source.title: Batch Normalization Biases Residual Blocks Towards the Identity Function in Deep Networks

record.tranche_reason: Compares normalized residual networks with residual downscaling and other training conditions, reporting training losses and learning-rate behavior relevant to V3 and V6.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 training-loss results by depth and describes CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 batch-size comparisons. It does not report training classification error, corrupted or random labels, or results for plain networks without shortcuts. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests V6's learning-rate tolerance component: batch-normalized residual networks tolerate larger learning rates than SkipInit and ordinary unnormalized networks. Its endpoint training losses do not directly measure training classification error, depth degradation of that error, or accuracy gain speed.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors identify residual branches being biased toward the identity at initialization as batch normalization's primary deep-ResNet trainability benefit, recover it with SkipInit, and distinguish larger stable learning rates from their practical usefulness, which is concentrated at large batch sizes. They also identify a separate regularization benefit.
record.recipe_differences: Tests residual-network depth and training-loss behavior using batch normalization, SkipInit and other residual scaling conditions; reports CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 results rather than classification-error results.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth, residual-branch initialization/scaling, L2 regularization, batch size, and batch-statistics procedure affect the reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Batch normalization and sufficiently downscaled SkipInit residual branches achieve very low training cross-entropy at depth 1000; unscaled residual branches fail to train.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deep residual-network low-loss trainability depends on residual-branch scaling at initialization and can be recovered without normalization using SkipInit.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed 200-epoch budget, ordinary unnormalized networks have higher training loss than batch-normalized networks, while SkipInit has lower loss than batch normalization at small batch sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effect of normalization on endpoint training cross-entropy depends on the unnormalized initialization recipe and batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: At small batch sizes, optimal learning rates are similar across methods and well below their maximum stable rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Greater learning-rate tolerance provides practical optimization benefits mainly at large batch sizes under a fixed epoch budget.

record.problems: Training classification error is not reported; the main batch-size comparisons are plotted without numerical values in the supplied text. CIFAR-10 depth results use the best 5 of 7 runs; ImageNet experiments use a single run per learning rate, but ImageNet results do not directly test the listed versions.
record.rows_left_out: Other CIFAR-10 depths and methods in Table 3 and CIFAR-100 depth/method combinations in Table 6 are not included; the retained rows cover the depth-1000 success and failure conditions, plus the BN and SkipInit comparison relevant to V6. Figure-only batch-size results are retained where the text explicitly describes the outcome.

untested.parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and the stated model-size, early-stopping and regularization qualifications; only training cross-entropy is reported.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.

Training classification-error degradation in plain batch-normalized networks versus identity-shortcut networks, including longer training; plain tanh initialization and the specific Fixup trainability result.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons in plain networks, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks.
Initial linearized stability thresholds, catapult recovery, curvature dynamics and full-batch edge-of-stability behavior.
Accuracy gain speed over training time or updates, and Fixup matching batch normalization's training speed and stability. Fixed-epoch validation accuracies do not establish these.

missing.what: CIFAR-100 confirmation that batch normalization permits larger stable learning rates and larger-batch training than SkipInit and Regularized SkipInit.
missing.locator: Appendix E, Figure 7 and accompanying text; 28-10 Wide-ResNet, 200 epochs, ghost batch size 32

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. No challenge follows from small-batch learning-rate similarity: optimal rates and maximum stable rates are different quantities. Training-loss rows are retained as related findings rather than treated as direct measurements of classification error or accuracy gain speed. Depth experiments summarize selected successful runs, so they do not establish success rates across all initializations.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, including corrupted or random labels and model-size/early-stopping conditions.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and student width relative to teacher width.

The plain-network versus shortcut comparison, ImageNet, and training classification error are not tested. The study tests residual-network depth, batch normalization, residual scaling, and training loss.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and very deep plain networks.
Training above the stability limit and sharpness dynamics.
Accuracy gain speed over training time is not measured. The study compares batch-size-dependent training losses and learning-rate behavior in residual networks.

rows.subject: n-2 Wide-ResNet with batch normalization
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 for 200 epochs; minimum training cross-entropy reported.
rows.note: Reported as the minimum training loss over the learning-rate search.
rows.check: The value matches Table 3, but minimum cross-entropy after 200 epochs does not directly measure V3's training classification-error degradation.

rows.subject: n-2 Wide-ResNet with batch normalization
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 for 200 epochs; minimum training cross-entropy reported.

rows.subject: n-2 Wide-ResNet with SkipInit (α = 1)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 for 200 epochs without downscaling the residual branch.
rows.note: The paper reports no result because training failed; Table 1 says such cases were omitted when test accuracy remained frozen at random initialization across the learning-rate grid.
rows.check: This condition removes batch normalization and residual downscaling; it is outside V3's batch-normalized comparison. The dash denotes training failure across the searched learning rates, not a numerical training loss.

rows.subject: n-2 Wide-ResNet with SkipInit (α = 0)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 for 200 epochs without L2 regularization; minimum training cross-entropy reported.
rows.note: The paper states L2 regularization is not necessary for trainability.
rows.check: The value matches Table 3, but SkipInit without L2 is neither the batch-normalized residual recipe nor the specific Fixup recipe named in the versions.

rows.subject: n-2 Wide-ResNet with residual block divided by √2
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with each residual block output divided by √2.
rows.note: The table reports no result for this condition; the text says merely stabilizing forward activations is insufficient for trainability.
rows.check: Dividing the merged block output by square root of two scales the skip path as well, so this is not V3's identity-shortcut condition. The dash represents failed training, not a measured loss.

rows.subject: n-2 Wide-ResNet with batch normalization
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-100 for 200 epochs; minimum training loss reported.
rows.note: The table reports the minimum training loss over the learning-rate search.
rows.check: The value matches Table 6, but endpoint cross-entropy on CIFAR-100 does not directly measure V3's training classification-error comparison.

rows.subject: n-2 Wide-ResNet with SkipInit (α = 0)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-100 for 200 epochs; minimum training loss reported.
rows.note: The table reports the minimum training loss over the learning-rate search.
rows.check: The value matches Table 6. SkipInit is a different normalization-free recipe from Fixup, and the measure is endpoint loss.

rows.subject: n-2 Wide-ResNet with SkipInit (α = 1)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-100 without downscaling the residual branch.
rows.note: No training-loss result is reported for this condition; the text says depth-1000 networks cannot be trained without downscaling residual-branch activations.
rows.check: Unnormalized, unscaled residual branches are outside V3's batch-normalized condition. The text explicitly identifies training failure; the dash is not a numerical loss.

rows.subject: 16-4 Wide-ResNet with batch normalization
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss across batch sizes after 200 epochs.
rows.baseline: SkipInit and unnormalized networks at the same batch sizes
rows.value: Batch normalization has better training-set performance at all batch sizes, according to the text; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The text says normalized-network performance is better on the training set at all batch sizes; precise values are not stated in text.
rows.check: The baseline is wrong: the all-batch-size training-loss advantage is over ordinary unnormalized networks, not SkipInit. SkipInit has lower loss in the small-batch regime. Endpoint loss does not measure V6's accuracy gain speed.

rows.subject: 16-4 Wide-ResNet with SkipInit
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss and optimal learning rate across batch sizes after 200 epochs.
rows.baseline: batch normalization at the same batch sizes
rows.value: SkipInit achieves smaller training losses than batch normalization for batch sizes b < 1024, according to the text; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: This comparison shows that batch normalization does not have lower training loss in this stated batch-size range.
rows.check: The textual comparison is correct, with the boundary approximately b ≤ 1024. Lower endpoint loss for SkipInit does not establish reversed accuracy gain speed, and SkipInit is not Fixup.

rows.subject: 16-4 Wide-ResNet with batch normalization
rows.operation_detail: Compared maximum stable learning rates across batch sizes.
rows.value: Batch normalized networks have a larger maximum stable learning rate than SkipInit networks, which have a larger maximum stable learning rate than unnormalized networks; figure only for values.
rows.note: The text explicitly states the ordering; it also says optimal learning rates are much smaller than the maximum stable rate when batch size is small.
rows.check: The text explicitly confirms the stable-learning-rate ordering. Figures 3(c,d) plot optimal learning rates rather than a separate numerical sweep of maximum stable rates; retain the ordering as textual evidence.
